title: Study Notes – Cell: The Unit of Life
overview: Comprehensive revision notes covering the fundamentals of cell biology, historical development, cell theory, cell structure, and key distinctions between plant and animal cells, designed for Class 11 biology and NEET preparation.

subtopics.title: Key Biological Facts
subtopics.content:
Cell: Structural & functional unit of life.
Mitochondria: Powerhouse of the cell.
ATP: Energy currency.
Bryophytes: Amphibians of the plant kingdom.
important_points: Cell is the basic unit of life

subtopics.title: Definition of a Living Organism
subtopics.content:
Presence of cells is the defining feature.
Living vs. non‑living: Humans, plants, bacteria have cells; microphones, pens do not.
Viruses are not considered living because they lack their own cell.

subtopics.title: Unicellular vs. Multicellular Organisms
subtopics.content:
Multicellular: Humans (billions of cells) – complex tissues & organs.
Unicellular: Bacteria, protozoans – single cell performs all life functions.
NCERT Quote: “The structure of bacteria is very simple.”
Bacteria (Prokaryotes): No membrane‑bound organelles, no well‑developed nucleus, high metabolic diversity, independent existence.
important_points: Unicellular organisms perform all functions in one cell

subtopics.title: Discovery of the Cell
subtopics.content: First cell observed in bark of *Quercus suber* (oak). Note: The first cell discovered was **not** a living cell.
important_points: First cell observed in oak bark

subtopics.title: Advancements in Microscopy (1950s–1960s)
subtopics.content:
Electron microscope breakthroughs (1950–1960) enabled visualization of structures previously invisible.
Key Discoveries Post‑1950:
- Ribosomes: 15–20 nm (1953)
- Cell membrane: Gradual understanding (1950)
- Fluid‑mosaic model: 1972 (Singer & Nicolson) – final model of plasma membrane

subtopics.title: Cell Theory Postulates
subtopics.content:
Scientist | Year | Key Contribution | Scope
--- | --- | --- | ---
Matthias Schleiden | 1838 | Plants composed of cells forming tissues | Plants only
Theodor Schwann | 1839 | All animals & plants made of cells; identified cell membrane & wall | All organisms
Rudolf Virchow | 1855 | “Omnis cellula‑e cellula” – new cells arise from pre‑existing cells | All organisms

Postulates:
1. All living organisms are made of cells or products of cells.
2. New cells arise from pre‑existing cells.

flashcards.question: What is the basic structural and functional unit of life?
What organelle is referred to as the "powerhouse" of the cell?
What molecule is considered the energy currency of the cell?
How do unicellular and multicellular organisms differ in terms of cellular organization?
flashcards.answer: Unicellular organisms perform all life functions in a single cell, whereas multicellular organisms have many specialized cells forming tissues and organs.

flashcards.question: Why are viruses not classified as living organisms?
flashcards.answer: Because they lack a cellular structure and cannot carry out metabolic processes independently.

flashcards.question: What key cellular feature distinguishes prokaryotes from eukaryotes?
flashcards.answer: Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles and a well‑developed nucleus.

flashcards.question: Where was the first cell observed and what was notable about it?
flashcards.answer: In the bark of Quercus suber (oak); it was not a living cell.

flashcards.question: What technological advancement in the 1950s–1960s allowed scientists to visualize ribosomes and the cell membrane?
flashcards.answer: The electron microscope, which revealed ribosomes (15–20 nm) in 1953 and contributed to understanding the cell membrane.

flashcards.question: What is the fluid‑mosaic model of the plasma membrane?
flashcards.answer: A model proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972 describing the membrane as a fluid bilayer with embedded proteins moving laterally.

flashcards.question: What are the two main postulates of the cell theory?
flashcards.answer: 1) All living organisms are made of cells or products of cells. 2) New cells arise from pre‑existing cells.

flashcards.question: Why does Rudolf Virchow state that new cells arise from pre‑existing cells?
flashcards.answer: Because cellular division is the only way to increase cell number, ensuring continuity of life processes.

flashcards.question: What type of plants are bryophytes?
flashcards.answer: Bryophytes are non‑vascular plants such as mosses.
